description: 5 should-trigger + 5 should-not-trigger queries. Should-trigger covers pasting a source URL/repo to check its license before borrowing, and asking whether a specific borrow is allowed. Should-not-trigger covers near-miss neighbours (regenerating notices, running a broad similarity scan, generic new-dependency intake, plain code review) whose vocabulary overlaps.

queries.q: I want to adapt this retry-loop from https://github.com/example/repo — is its license compatible with ours?
this Stack Overflow answer has the algorithm I need, check if I can use it before I write the code
can I borrow this LRU cache implementation, it's under GPL-3.0?
draft a ledger entry for the debounce helper I ported from another repo
what license does this vendored snippet carry and does it clear our policy?
regenerate the third-party notices file, the ledger just changed
run a similarity scan across the whole diff to check for copied code
queries.note: broad corpus scan, no single named source → license-compliance-audit

queries.q: add lodash to package.json and install it
queries.note: new dependency intake, not a code borrow → supply-chain-intake

queries.q: review this diff for correctness and style issues
queries.note: generic code review, no borrow involved

queries.q: what CVEs affect the version of this package we're pinned to?
queries.note: dependency vulnerability scanning, not licensing a borrow
